status_badge.copy_diagnostics_hint: Copy the text or save it as a file, then send it with your chat problem report.

chat_engine.body: Whether the local chat database and worker are ready. The green badge is the radio; loading and sending chats need this engine too. If chat is not working, first tap “{{action}}” below and paste the text into your report. ready = good. starting = still booting, with the time so far; if it stays there for more than a minute, one possible cause is a WebView running without JIT. failed = the error is shown below. idle = not asked to start yet (chat off or not signed in).
chat_engine.title: Chat engine

hubs.body: How many hub links are up right now. These are the TCP connections to community hubs. 0 means you are not on the mesh yet. 2 is typical and healthy.
hubs.title: Hubs

ifac.body: Interface Access Code size. This is the shared network filter derived from the mesh name. 16 B means you are on the named Qortal network. 0 B means the interface is open / unfiltered.
ifac.title: IFAC

known_paths.body: How many destinations Reticulum currently has a route to. Each announce teaches the phone a way to reach an identity. A few hundred is normal on a busy mesh. This is not live chat.
known_paths.title: Known paths

network_name.body: The Reticulum mesh this phone joined. Qortal’s public mesh is qortal-hub. A different name means you are on a different network and cannot see those peers.
network_name.title: Network name

online_accounts.body: How many Qortal accounts this phone currently sees as present on the mesh. Same number as Home. It is not the number of hubs or Reticulum nodes.
online_accounts.title: Online accounts

received.body: Total data this phone has received from the hubs since Reticulum started this session. It resets when the stack restarts, not when you close a chat.
received.title: Received

sent.body: Total data this phone has sent to the hubs since Reticulum started this session. It resets when the stack restarts, not when you close a chat.
sent.title: Sent
